# Guardhouse console paint

Generated with the built-in image-generation tool on October 9, 2026. This is the saved project asset; no runtime dependency on the generator or the original output directory.

## Final prompt

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production painterly texture atlas for simple low-polygon 3D guardhouse computer and telephone consoles in Animal Factory Tactics.
Create ONE square 2048x2048 opaque bitmap containing exactly 4 columns by 4 rows of equal square texture panels, flush to the canvas edges. No gutters, no written cell labels, no background surrounding the grid. Each panel occupies exactly one quarter of the width and height. Every panel is a flat orthographic surface viewed square-on, never a perspective illustration of a whole object.
Style: hand-painted tactical-game equipment. Confident broad brush strokes, clear graphic edges, warm bright highlights, dark painted seams, subtle dry-brush scuffs. Olive/sage painted steel, warm ivory computer plastic, charcoal-black bakelite telephone, restrained green/amber phosphor displays. Readable and maintained with modest edge wear, NOT heavily rusted or covered in mud. All screws, buttons, vents, keycaps and scratches are painted into flat surfaces, not modeled depth. No logos or decorative text.
Row 1 left to right:
1. plain sage olive painted steel swatch, brushwork and a few small scuffs, no panels or hardware;
2. warm ivory molded plastic swatch with painted edge light and subtle grime, no hardware;
3. charcoal black bakelite swatch, broad dark-grey painterly highlights, no hardware;
4. dark desaturated green worktop swatch with lightly worn edges, no hardware.
Row 2 left to right:
1. CRT monitor FRONT: centered rectangular dark green screen, simple pale-green map schematic and a few short scanline-like data marks; thick ivory bezel fills panel edge to edge; tiny painted power switch below;
2. second CRT monitor FRONT: centered dark screen with amber grid and simple tracking diagram, same ivory bezel and painted power switch;
3. computer keyboard TOP: five straight rows of broad ivory keycaps and a long spacebar in a dark green rectangular tray; slightly exaggerated painted shadows make the keys readable;
4. vintage desk telephone base TOP: black bakelite telephone base surface with a large cream circular rotary dial occupying the LOWER TWO THIRDS; at the top only two simple cradle recesses; NO handset (the handset will be separate geometry).
Row 3 left to right:
1. sage cabinet FRONT with two doors, a narrow central seam, two small painted metal latch handles, modest lower vents, highlighted outer edges;
2. sage cabinet SIDE with one recessed painted rectangular service panel and shallow horizontal vent slots, no protrusions;
3. flat olive radio control FACE with a cream analogue meter, dark speaker grille, small ivory knobs and tiny red/green indicator dots, all painted and readable;
4. sage cabinet FRONT with two wide stacked drawers, painted dark recessed handles and bright worn edge lines.
Row 4 left to right:
1. ivory CRT casing BACK with broad black ventilation slits and one small painted service plate;
2. charcoal black handset material swatch with lengthwise hand-painted grey highlights, no dial or buttons, NO silhouette on a background;
3. cream control-panel FACE with simple four-by-three dark square buttons and a small red status light;
4. plain sage enamel service panel with four painted corner screws and bright upper-edge wear, for the computer base.
Constraints: exact regular 4x4 layout; objects/surfaces centered within each cell; important features at least 5% inset from cell edges. Lighting painted from upper left, no cast shadows outside a cell. No photographic realism, no sci-fi neon, no shiny plastic or metal reflections, no 3D scene, no perspective, no watermark.
